title: Amortized Molecular Optimization via Group Relative Policy Optimization
claim: Per-input search loops pay costly oracle calls every time; a policy trained once offline generates answers with zero oracle calls.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, dashed divider, clock icons marking cost
description: Two horizontal flow diagrams stacked and separated by a dashed line. Panel A, Search-Based / Instance Optimization, runs left to right: a purple Input Structure box, a gray Generation Phase container holding a blue Generate Candidates box and a thick red Call Oracle box with a red stopwatch, then a tan Final Molecules box. A feedback arrow loops from the oracle back to candidate generation. A caption notes high latency and oracle cost per input. Panel B, Amortized Optimization, has a gray Offline Training Phase (One-Time) container with Sample Structures, Generate Candidates, Call Oracle (red, stopwatch) and an orange Update Policy box, plus a feedback loop. It leads to a second gray Generation Phase with Input Structure and Policy Forward Pass, then a green clock labeled Zero Oracle Calls and Final Molecules. Red marks cost, green marks savings, and the eye goes first to the red oracle boxes.
caption: Comparison of optimization paradigms. (A) Instance Optimization: Requires an expensive iterative search with hundreds to thousands of oracle calls for every new input structure Si, resulting in high cost that scales linearly with library size. (B) Amortized Optimization: Front-loads computation into offline training. The learned policy πθ generates optimized molecules for new, unseen inputs Si in a single rollout without inference-time oracle calls, enabling scalable, highthroughput design.
abstract: In structurally constrained molecular optimization, state-of-the-art methods treat every new input structure as a separate instance, restarting an expensive oracle-driven search from scratch and scaling poorly to settings with many starting structures or expensive oracles. While amortized approaches that learn a transferable policy could in principle remove this bottleneck, existing methods struggle to generalize to diverse structural constraints at inference time. We present AMORTIX, a Graph Transformer model that natively supports such constraints, optimizing molecular structures in a single rollout with zero inference-time oracle calls. A central challenge for amortized training in this domain is that optimization difficulty varies drastically across starting structures. We address this by centering rewards within groups of completions that share the same starting structure. We evaluate on goal-directed scaffold decoration, including single- and multi-target kinase inhibitor design, and on a few-shot prodrug case study. AMORTIX outperforms both amortized baselines and search-based instance optimizers on kinase scaffold decoration, and ablations across 23 objectives show that group-relative centering improves over REINFORCE and PPO and is substantially more consistent across scaffold splits. The prodrug case study further demonstrates transfer of learned modification rules to unseen drug structures.
